sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Checker setup and rules
sections.what: Imports the shared vocabulary and the matcher, and states that the checker reads and writes nothing.
sections.why: The header says that pure input and output makes the gate testable and rerunnable.
sections.watch_out: Adding any database call here breaks that promise.

sections.name: E25Input
sections.title: Checker input shape
sections.what: Defines the four inputs: artifact, mode, numerals, and the snapshot.
sections.why: Gives the checker one clear bundle of everything it needs.

sections.name: classify (part 1)
sections.title: Checking derived numbers
sections.what: A derived number is computed only if a calculation record exists and its stored value matches the number. Otherwise it is untraceable.
sections.why: The comment says the arithmetic is the claim, and evidence behind the inputs does not prove the arithmetic.
sections.watch_out: A derived number with no calculation record always fails, even if its inputs are well sourced.

sections.name: classify: if
sections.title: Checking reported numbers against sources
sections.what: For a reported number, collects its linked evidence. No linked evidence means untraceable. If a source passage contains the number, it is sourced. Client supplied evidence is accepted when no passage matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: the spec admits uploaded files as their own class, so they are not counted as failures.
sections.watch_out: Passages are checked before client supplied evidence, so a row that has both is judged by its passages first.

sections.name: classify: if
sections.title: Last checks for reported numbers
sections.what: If a client supplied row exists, the number is client supplied. Otherwise it is untraceable because its passages do not contain the number.
sections.why: This is the final fallback that decides the cause.
sections.watch_out: The explanation reports how many passages were compared but not the text that was compared, so it is hard to see why a match failed.

sections.name: validateNumericProvenance
sections.title: Building the final report
sections.what: Classifies every number, counts each class, computes rates, tallies causes and labels, and sets pass or fail. A pass needs at least one number and a traceable rate at or above the threshold.
sections.why: The report gives a rate and distance, not a bare result.
sections.watch_out: The report sets wouldBlock whether or not the mode blocks, so it is shown even in warn mode.

summary: The checker: it sorts every number in an artifact into computed, sourced, client supplied, or untraceable, and then reports the rates and whether the gate passes.
purpose: Decides for each number whether the app can show proof of where it came from.
why: The header says it is pure, meaning it reads nothing from outside, so it can be tested with fixed inputs and rerun on stored artifacts later.
how: For each number, checks derived numbers against a calculation record. For reported numbers, looks for linked evidence, then for a source passage containing the number, then for client supplied evidence. Any number that fails gets a cause. Then it counts results, computes rates, tallies causes and labels, and decides pass or fail.
inputs: The artifact reference, the mode, the list of numerals, and the snapshot of evidence and calculations.
risks: Client supplied numbers count toward the traceable rate, so unverified uploads can raise the score. An artifact with no numbers fails, which is correct but may surprise a reader.
debug: Read the explanation attached to each untraceable number. Confirm that the linked IDs exist in the snapshot. Check the unit hint if a number that should match does not.
